body.text: There is a prayer in the thirty third chapter of Exodus that has followed me for the better part of my life, and it has never let me go. Moses prayed it after he had already seen more of God than any man living in his day. He had stood before a bush that burned and was not consumed. He had watched a river turn to blood and a nation of slaves walk free in a single night. He had lifted a rod over the sea and seen the water stand up on both sides like walls. He had eaten bread that fell from the sky. And after all of that, this is what he asked for:

lines: Now therefore, I pray thee, if I have found grace in thy sight, shew me now thy way, that I may know thee, that I may find grace in thy sight: and consider that this nation is thy people.

body.text: Read it slowly, because everything in this book hangs on that one sentence. Moses did not ask for another miracle. He did not ask for a bigger crowd, a stronger arm, or a faster deliverance. He asked for the ways of God, and he told God exactly why he wanted them. Shew me now thy way, that I may know thee. The ways were not the prize. Knowing God was the prize, and the ways were the road that led there.

Most of us have prayed for many things. We have prayed for open doors and closed doors, for healing, for children, for husbands, for jobs, for visas, for breakthrough. There is nothing wrong with any of those prayers, and God is not offended by them. But somewhere along the way we have to grow into the prayer Moses prayed, because it is the only prayer that ends in God Himself.
He Is Higher Than Our Reach
Before we go any further, we have to settle something that will humble us and set us free at the same time. The ways of God are past finding out.

lines: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

body.text: Paul was not complaining when he wrote that. He was worshipping. He had come to the end of his own understanding and instead of frustration he found praise. That is a mature place to arrive at, and many of us are still far from it.
You cannot fathom God. You cannot comprehend Him. His ways are so high that you cannot climb to them, and they are so deep that you will never touch the bottom. Hear how the Lord Himself says it:

lines: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.

body.text: Notice that He does not say His ways are slightly better than ours, or a little more advanced. He compares the distance between His ways and ours to the distance between the heavens and the earth. Stand outside tonight and look up. Whatever that distance is, that is the gap. You will not close it by being clever. You will not close it by reading one more book or attending one more conference, and I say that as a woman who loves books and conferences.

I have watched people wear themselves out trying to figure God out. They want a formula. They want a system that guarantees an outcome, so they can put in the coin and get the result. When God does not behave the way their system predicted, they are shaken, and some of them walk away from Him altogether. That is what happens when your relationship with God is built on your ability to predict Him.
Two Ditches On The Same Road
There are two ditches on this road and I want you to see both of them clearly.

The first ditch is the one I have just described. It is the attempt to reduce God to a formula. We take the ways of God and turn them into steps, and then we sell the steps. Seven keys to this, five principles for that. Some of that teaching is useful and I do not despise it, but no arrangement of principles will ever contain God. He is a person, not a machine, and persons are known through relationship, not through mastery.

The second ditch is the opposite one, and it is just as dangerous. It is the ditch of giving up. Somebody reads Isaiah 55 and concludes that since God is unsearchable there is no point searching at all. If He is that high, why bother reaching? So they settle for a distant God they do not expect to know, and they call their distance humility.
Both ditches miss the point. The fact that God's ways are past finding out is not a locked door. It is an open invitation.

lines: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.

body.text: God hides things the way a father hides a gift for his child, not the way an enemy hides a weapon. He conceals so that we will seek, and He counts it an honour when we come looking. The unsearchable God is the same God who told Moses to come up the mountain. He is the same God who said, draw nigh to me and I will draw nigh to you. The distance is real, but so is the invitation, and the invitation came from His side, not ours.
Why This Matters When Life Is Hard
Let me bring this down from the mountain and into your kitchen, because this is not theory.

Something has happened in your life that you cannot explain. A door closed that should have opened. Somebody died who should have lived. A prayer you prayed with all your strength was answered with silence, and you have been carrying a quiet question ever since. Why did God do it that way?

If you believe you are entitled to understand every one of God's dealings, then that unanswered question will grow into a wall between you and Him. But if you have settled in your heart that His ways are higher than yours, that same question becomes a door. You stop demanding an explanation and you start asking for Himself. You say, Lord, I do not understand this, and I may never understand it on this side, but I want to know You in it.

That is the difference between a believer who breaks under trouble and a believer who deepens under trouble. It is not that the second one suffered less. It is that the second one had already made peace with a God who is higher than her reasoning.
I am not asking you to pretend you understand. I am asking you to stop making understanding the condition of your trust.
The Prayer That Changes Everything

So we come back to Moses. He was standing at a hard place when he prayed that prayer. The people had made a golden calf while he was still on the mountain receiving the law. God had said He would send an angel with them instead of going Himself. Moses was leading a stubborn nation through a wilderness with no map, and in that pressure he did not ask for relief. He asked for the ways of God.

I want you to notice that Moses prayed this prayer as a man who already had a relationship with God. Verse eleven of that same chapter says the Lord spoke to him face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He was already a friend of God and he still wanted more. That is the mark of real intimacy. It never says, this is enough.

Some of us stopped growing years ago because we reached a level of God that satisfied us. We got the answer we needed, the marriage was restored, the business recovered, and we quietly stopped pressing. Moses had every reason to stop pressing and he pressed harder.
So let this be your prayer as you read on, and pray it out loud where you are:

lines: Oh God, if I have found grace in Your sight, shew me now Thy way.
Not Your works only, but Your ways.
Not Your hand only, but Your heart.
Shew me Thy way, that I may know Thee.

body.text: You are powerful, Lord, so powerful in Your ways. And You are glorious, so glorious in Your ways.
If God answers that prayer for you, and He will, you will come out of this book a different woman and a different man than you went in.
I want to show you a verse that divides the church into two groups. It is one verse, it is short, and once you see what is inside it you will never read it the same way again.

lines: He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.

body.text: Look at it carefully. Two parties are named in one sentence. Moses is one. The children of Israel are the other. Two different things were given to them. Moses received the ways of God. Israel received the acts of God. Same God, same wilderness, same forty years, and two completely different levels of knowing.
This is the whole matter. There are two levels at which a human being can know God, and where you live between those two levels will determine almost everything about your walk with Him.
The First Level: Knowing His Works

The first level is knowing God's works. This is knowing what He does. His acts, His miracles, His signs and wonders, His interventions and provisions. Many believers are at this level, and I want to be careful here, because this level is not evil. It is real, and God Himself gives it.

Look at what Israel actually saw. They watched ten plagues fall on the greatest empire of their day. They walked through a sea on dry ground. For forty years they ate bread that appeared on the ground every morning, and when they cried for meat, quails came in from the sea. Water came out of a rock. A pillar of cloud covered them by day and a pillar of fire lit their camp by night, for forty years without one night off. Their clothes did not wear out and their shoes did not wear out, and if you have ever tried to keep shoes on a growing child you know what kind of miracle that is.
And look at the state of their bodies when they came out:

lines: He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes.

body.text: Not one feeble person. Millions of people came out of four hundred years of slavery and there was not one weak person among them. No arthritis limping out of Egypt. No one carried on a stretcher. That is a work of God and it is glorious.

Let me stop the teaching for a moment and prophesy, because the God who did that has not changed. The God of Israel is taking away feebleness, weakness and sickness from somebody reading this page today, in the name of Jesus. That thing that has made you slow and tired and afraid of your own body, He is removing it. Receive it now.

And there is more in that verse. He brought them forth also with silver and gold. They did not walk out empty. They walked out of the house of slavery carrying the wealth of the nation that had enslaved them, and God had arranged it in advance.

lines: And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty.
And the LORD gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants, and in the sight of the people.

body.text: Somebody reading this is retiring soon, and there is so much fear in your heart. You have done the arithmetic and the arithmetic frightens you. Hear the word of the Lord. You are not leaving empty handed. The favour that came upon Israel, that made Egyptians hand over their gold and silver, is coming upon you in the name of Jesus. The silver is His and the gold is His, and He knows where all of it is kept.

lines: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.

body.text: So please hear me clearly. I am not writing this book to talk you out of miracles. Some of you will see the works of God this very week, and you will believe, and you will know Him better because of it. God still heals, He still provides, He still opens doors that ten men could not open. His works are real and His works are good.
The problem is not the works. The problem is stopping there.
The Second Level: Knowing His Ways

The second level is knowing God's ways. This is not knowing what He does. It is knowing who He is. It is understanding how He thinks, what He loves, what He hates, how He moves, why He waits, what He is after in the long run. It is the difference between knowing that a man gives good gifts and knowing the man himself.
Moses had this. Israel did not. And the results of that difference are written all over the rest of the Bible.

Israel saw the acts of God and stayed a nation of complainers. They saw the Red Sea open and three days later they were murmuring about water. They ate manna in the morning and complained about it by evening. They saw fire on the mountain and made a calf at the bottom of it. Miracles did not mature them. Forty years of continuous supernatural provision produced a generation that God said had not known His ways, and that generation died in the wilderness.

Moses knew the ways of God and he stood in the gap for the very people who were driving him mad. When God said He would destroy them and make a great nation out of Moses instead, Moses said no. A man who only knew God's acts would have taken the offer. A man who knew God's ways knew what God actually wanted, and he asked God to be who He is.
That is what knowing the ways does. It lets you agree with God about His own heart.
What The Difference Looks Like Today
Let me make this practical, because the two levels are alive and well in the church right now.

The believer who only knows God's works lives on evidence. When the evidence is good, her faith is loud. When the evidence dries up, her faith goes quiet, and she starts looking for someone with fresher evidence. She moves from church to church in search of the works of God. She goes wherever the newest testimony is, and when that place goes through a dry season she moves again. She has been a Christian for twenty years and she is still a spiritual visitor, belonging to no one, planted nowhere.

The believer who knows God's ways lives on God's character. She has trouble like everybody else, but her trouble does not move her foundation, because her foundation was never the evidence. She can go through a season with no visible answer and still worship, because she is not confused about who God is. She has a stability that the first believer envies and does not understand.
You can tell them apart most clearly in the waiting. Anyone can rejoice when the answer comes. It is in the long silence that you find out which level a person is living on.
Where Are You?
So I want you to be honest with yourself. Not with me, and not with your pastor. With yourself.

Which of these describes you? When you think about God, do you mostly think about what He has done for you and what you are waiting for Him to do? Or do you think about who He is, apart from what He gives?
If you have been at the first level, do not be condemned. Every one of us starts there. God is not angry with you for beginning where everyone begins. He is inviting you to grow.

The rest of this book is about that growth. And I tell you plainly, it is better to know His ways than His works, because when you know His ways the works will follow anyway. Israel was busy admiring the miracles while Moses was busy being the man through whom the miracles came. Which of the two do you want to be?
I want to ask you a question and I want you to sit with it before you answer. Are you following Jesus, or are you serving Him for the bread and the fish?
Do not answer quickly. That question has exposed more people than any sermon I have ever preached, and it has exposed me too, more than once.
The Generation That Sought A Sign

In the days of Jesus there was a whole crowd of people who wanted to see something. They followed Him from town to town, but they were not following Him. They were following the display. Listen to how He answered them:

lines: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas.

body.text: That is strong language, and it came out of the mouth of the gentlest man who ever lived. He called sign seeking evil and adulterous. Why such hard words? Because adultery is what you call it when someone wants the benefits of a covenant without the covenant. They wanted His power without His person, and He named it for what it was.

We have our own version of it today. We hear that a certain prophet is in town, and the whole city empties into one hall. Next month a different name is announced and the same crowd moves there. People will travel for hours and spend money they do not have to see the newest sign and wonder, and the same people will not spend twenty quiet minutes alone with God in their own bedroom.

I am not against gifted men and women. God gives them, and I honour them. But if your walk with God consists of running from one manifestation to another, you are not following Jesus. You are following an experience, and experiences run out.
He Did Not Commit Himself To Them
Here is a passage that should sober all of us. It is short and most people read past it.

lines: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did. But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men, and needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

body.text: Do you see what happened there? People believed in Him. The Bible says so plainly. Their belief was real enough to be recorded. And yet Jesus did not commit Himself to them.

He would not entrust Himself to a faith that was built on miracles, because He knew what such faith is worth when the miracles stop. He had seen it before. A crowd that gathers for bread will scatter for hunger, and He was not going to build His work on people like that.

Let me say this as plainly as I know how. If you are a miracle seeker, God does not take you seriously. He will still be kind to you, He will still heal you and provide for you because that is His nature, but He will not commit Himself to you. He will not share His secrets with you. He will not entrust you with His heart. There are levels of God's confidence that are simply closed to the person who only wants what God can do.
And I want that to bother you enough to change something.
Forty Years Of Miracles And No Rest
Now let me take you to the most frightening passage on this subject in the whole Bible. The writer of Hebrews is quoting the story of Israel in the wilderness and applying it to us.

lines: Wherefore as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: when your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.

body.text: Take that passage apart with me slowly, because it holds the thesis of this entire book.

They saw my works forty years. Forty years of unbroken miracles. Not one dry week. Bread every morning, fire every night, a cloud every day, water from rocks, shoes that would not wear out. If a long exposure to the supernatural could change a heart, that generation would have been the most transformed generation in history.
They have not known my ways. Forty years of works and they still did not know His ways. That is the diagnosis, and it came from God Himself.

They shall not enter into my rest. That is the verdict, and it is terrifying. People who see the works of God only, and never come to know His ways, do not enter His rest. They wander. They live in a state of permanent spiritual restlessness, always seeking, never settled, always at the next meeting looking for the next thing, and they die in the wilderness within sight of the promise.
Read that verdict again and let it search you. It is possible to be surrounded by the supernatural and still be a stranger to God. It is possible to have testimonies and no rest.
The Crowd That Left
There is one more scene I must show you, and it is the one that tells the truth about crowds.

Jesus had fed five thousand men with a boy's lunch. The next day the same crowd came looking for Him, and He told them the truth about themselves. He said they were not seeking Him because of the miracles but because they ate of the loaves and were filled. Then instead of feeding them again, He began to talk about something deeper.

lines: I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat? Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you. Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

body.text: He was talking about fellowship. He was talking about intimacy, about taking Him into yourself until He becomes part of you the way food becomes part of the body that eats it. He moved the conversation from lunch to union.
And the crowd could not follow Him there.

lines: From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

body.text: They came for bread and they left over intimacy. As long as He was handing out fish they were the most devoted congregation in Galilee. The moment He started talking about eating His flesh and drinking His blood, about a real and costly union with Himself, the hall emptied.

Understand what Jesus did there. He did not chase them. He did not soften the message to keep the numbers. He let the shallow go, and then He turned to the twelve and asked whether they would leave too. He was not building a crowd. He was building friends.
Which One Are You?
So the question comes back around, and now you have enough light to answer it honestly.
Are you following Jesus, or are you serving Him for the bread and the fish?
If you found out today that God would never do another miracle for you as long as you live, but you could know Him more deeply than you have ever known Him, would you still want Him?

That question is not fair and I know it. But your answer to it tells you exactly where you live. And if the answer that came up in your heart embarrassed you, then thank God for the light, because now you know what to pray about.

I have made my choice, and I made it a long time ago. I choose the way of the Lord. Not the bread and the fish. Not the crowd and the noise. I want the One who gives the bread. And in the next chapter I want to show you what that choice actually costs, and what it is worth.

label: Chapter Four
title: I Choose The Way Of The Lord

body.text: Everything I have written so far has been leading you to a decision. Now the decision has to be made, because knowing about the two levels changes nothing until you choose one of them.
I choose the way of the Lord. I want you to say it out loud where you are sitting. I choose the way of the Lord.
That sentence sounds simple and it is not. It costs something, and I would be dishonest with you if I pretended otherwise. So let me tell you what it costs, and then let me tell you what it is worth.
The Cost Of Choosing
The first thing this choice costs you is the thrill of the crowd.

When you decide that you want the ways of God more than the works of God, you stop being at the centre of every exciting thing. The meetings will still be full and you will not always be in them. People around you will still be running to the newest thing, and you will be at home with your Bible open, and there will be evenings when that feels very small and very quiet. Nobody claps for the woman who chose the quiet room.

The second thing it costs is speed. The works of God can come to you in a night. The ways of God are learned over years. You cannot download the ways of God. Moses spent forty years in Pharaoh's house and forty years behind a desert with sheep before God ever spoke to him from a bush, and then another forty years learning God in the wilderness. Abraham waited twenty five years for one son. If you want something fast, this is not the road.

The third thing it costs is control. As long as you are dealing with God on the level of works, you can keep a kind of distance and a kind of management. You bring your request, He answers, life continues. When you ask for His ways you are asking Him to change how you think, and God does not do that gently. He will touch things you were not planning to give Him.
What It Is Worth
Now let me tell you what you get, and I say this as a witness and not as a theorist.

You get rest. Remember what God said about the generation that never knew His ways. They shall not enter into my rest. Turn the sentence over and the promise appears. Those who know His ways enter His rest. There is a settledness that comes into a person who has learned how God moves, and it does not leave when circumstances change.

You get stability. You stop being blown around by every report and every prophecy and every rumour. You are no longer running from place to place, panicking, asking everyone you meet what they think God is doing. You know Him, so you have a place to stand.

You get accuracy. When you know the ways of a person you can predict what will please them without being told each time. A wife who knows her husband does not need a list. This is why God could trust Moses with decisions in the wilderness. Moses knew Him well enough to represent Him.

And you get the works anyway. This is what people miss. Choosing the ways does not mean losing the works, it means receiving them from a different place. While Israel was busy admiring miracles, Moses was busy being the man through whom the miracles came. God said it plainly to me one day and I have never recovered from it. I want to give you more than miracles, I want to make you a miracle worker. I want to make you the sign and the wonder.
That is the exchange on the table. You give up the excitement of chasing and you receive the authority of knowing.
The Warning I Cannot Leave Out
I would not be a faithful writer if I gave you only the sweet part of this, so hear the hard part too.
There is a scene at the end of the Sermon on the Mount that should shake every one of us who works in ministry.

lines: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

body.text: Look at who is being addressed there. Read the verses before it. These are not unbelievers. These are people who prophesied in His name, cast out devils in His name, and did many wonderful works in His name. They had works. They had ministry. They had results that any church would celebrate. And the Lord said, I never knew you.
He did not say, you never worked for me. He said, I never knew you. The whole issue was knowing, and it was mutual knowing that was missing.
It is possible to spend a lifetime as a stranger to God and expect to spend eternity with Him. May that not be our portion. May we not hear the Master say at the end, I know you not, depart from me.

I do not write that to frighten you into religion. I write it because the sure way of getting recognition in the end is by knowing the ways of God, and there is no shortcut around it. Not gifting. Not anointing. Not attendance. Not even fruitfulness. Knowing.
Of All The Knowledge In The World

We live in an age that worships knowledge. People give their entire youth to degrees and certifications, and I am not against any of it. Get the education, be excellent, be the best in your field. But of all the knowledge this world offers, none of it surpasses the knowledge of God.

You can be brilliant and lost. You can master a subject and never know the One who made the subject. And here is the mercy in it. The knowledge of God is not reserved for the educated. Moses had the finest education in Egypt and Amos was a farmer, and God spoke to both of them. This door is open to a market woman in Aba and a professor in Cambridge on exactly the same terms.
You too can know Him. You too can be reconciled to Him. It is possible to know God's ways, and it is possible for you.
Make The Choice Now
So make the choice. Do not put the book down and mean to do it later, because later has swallowed more good intentions than open rebellion ever has.
Say it to Him where you are:

lines: Oh God, if You are pleased with me, teach me Your ways, that I may know You.
I choose Your ways over Your works.
I choose Your heart over Your hand.
I choose Your presence over Your presents.
I choose the way of the Lord.

body.text: Now, if you have never given your life to Jesus, I have to stop and say something to you before we go one page further. You cannot know the ways of a God you have not met. If you have only heard about Him, you do not know Him, and the ways are for those who know Him. Everything in this book assumes a relationship, so if that relationship is not there, begin there. Tell Him you are a sinner, tell Him you believe He died and rose again for you, ask Him to save you and to take over your life. He will not turn you away. And once He is your Lord, the rest of this book becomes yours.
Does God have favourites?
I have been asked that question many times and my answer is always the same. No, He does not have favourites, but He does have intimates. Those are not the same thing.

A favourite is chosen arbitrarily. An intimate is someone who came close. God is not partial, and the door to His inner circle is open to whoever will walk through it. But not everyone walks through it, and that is why the circle is small.
To some He shows His deeds. To those who qualify, He shows His ways. And I want to show you three people who qualified, so you can see exactly how a person becomes a friend of God.
Abraham, Called The Friend Of God
Three separate books of the Bible give Abraham the same title, and it is a title no one else carries so consistently.

lines: Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?
But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.
And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

body.text: The friend of God. Sit with that phrase. The Almighty, the One whose ways are past finding out, called a man from Ur His friend.
Now before you decide that Abraham was made of different material than you, let me remind you what is also written about him.

Abraham lied about his wife. Not once. Twice. He told Pharaoh that Sarah was his sister because he was afraid, and years later he did exactly the same thing to Abimelech. This is the father of faith, protecting himself with a lie and putting his wife at risk to do it.

Abraham took the Hagar alternative. God had promised him a son and the promise was taking too long, so he listened to his wife and produced a child by another woman, and the church is still living with the consequences of that decision.
Abraham doubted. He laughed. He argued. He asked God for signs. He did not arrive as a finished man.

And here is the good news buried in his failures. Abraham did not remain there. He grew. He grew in fellowship, he grew in intimacy, he grew in trust, until the God who had watched him lie and doubt and improvise called him friend.

The Abraham who fell for the Hagar arrangement is not the same Abraham who took his son up Mount Moriah. That was a different man. Look at what happened on that mountain. God spoke to him and he rose up early the next morning, no argument and no delay. Then he travelled three days. Three days is a long time. Three days is more than enough time to reconsider, to talk yourself out of it, to find a reason to turn back. And when he lifted his eyes on the third day and saw the place afar off, he kept walking.
That is not the man who lied in Egypt. That is a man who had come to know the ways of God well enough to trust Him with the very promise God had given.
So if you are discouraged about how far you still are, take heart. God is not looking for people who never fell. He is looking for people who did not remain where they fell.
The Man God Boasted About
Because Abraham had come that far, listen to what God says about him.

lines: And the LORD said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do; seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him? For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do justice and judgment.

body.text: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do. God was about to judge Sodom and He found Himself unwilling to do it without telling His friend. That is what intimacy produces. God let Abraham into His plans, and then let Abraham argue with Him about those plans, and honoured the argument.

And notice the reason God gives. For I know him. God knew what was in Abraham. He knew Abraham would raise his household in the way of the Lord. God was not guessing about His friend, He had studied him.
There is another man God spoke about this way, and He did it in front of the devil.

lines: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?

body.text: Hast thou considered my servant Job. God boasted about a man. He brought him up in conversation. He pointed to him as evidence.

So let me ask you the question that has kept me awake more than once. Does God know you? Not, do you know about God. Does He know you? And what does He know about you? If He were to speak about you the way He spoke about Abraham and Job, what would He say? Could He boast of you? What is His testimony concerning you?
Do not rush past those questions. Answer them.
Moses, Face To Face
The second friend is Moses, and his friendship is described in the most startling way in the Bible.

lines: And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.

body.text: As a man speaks to his friend. Not as a king speaks to a subject. Not as a general speaks to a soldier. As friends speak, with the ease and honesty and back and forth that friends have.

And what did that friendship produce? It produced the boldest praying in scripture. In the same chapter Moses says something that should astonish us. God had offered His presence, and Moses was not satisfied.

lines: And he said unto him, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.

body.text: Moses said, if You do not go with us Yourself, do not send us anywhere. He turned down the destination unless he could have the Person. Only a friend prays like that.

And then, still not satisfied, he asked for more. Shew me thy glory. Having spoken face to face, having received the promise of the presence, he asked to see the glory. Friendship with God never reaches a ceiling, because there is always more of Him.
Father, go with us in this nation. Thank You for Your presence. But Father, we need more than Your presence. Also go with us.
The Room Is Not Full
Now here is what I most want you to hear in this chapter, and I want you to receive it against every argument in your mind.
There is enough room in God's heart for everyone who wants to become His friend.

The circle of God's friends is not closed. Abraham did not take the last seat. Moses did not use up the position. David, who was a man after God's own heart, did not exhaust the supply. Jesus made this explicit to ordinary men who had failed Him repeatedly.

lines: Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.

body.text: Look at how He defines the difference between a servant and a friend. The servant does not know what his lord is doing. The friend is told. Friendship is measured by access to the heart, and Jesus opened that access to fishermen and tax collectors.
So the question is not whether there is room. The question is whether you want it enough to come.

I am a woman of the presence of God. I say that without apology. Like David, I have wanted His presence more than I have wanted anything else He could give, and I have shaped my life around that wanting. It is the best decision I have ever made, and it is available to you.
There is a chain in the life of a believer and every link of it hangs on the one before it. I want to lay the whole chain out in front of you first, and then we will take it link by link.

lines: To know God is to love Him.
To love God is to trust Him.
To trust God is to obey Him.
To obey God is to be blessed.

body.text: That is the order and the order cannot be rearranged. Most of the frustration in the church comes from people trying to start at the wrong end of that chain.
You Cannot Love What You Do Not Know
Everything begins with knowing, which is why the first five chapters of this book have been about knowing.

You cannot love a stranger. You can admire a stranger, you can fear a stranger, you can be impressed by a stranger, but you cannot love one. Love requires acquaintance. This is why so many believers struggle to love God in any real way. They are trying to love someone they have only heard about.

And this is why the enemy works so hard to keep your picture of God wrong. If he can make you believe God is harsh, or distant, or disappointed in you, or reluctant, then love becomes impossible and everything downstream collapses. Many people are obeying God out of fear because they never came to know Him well enough to love Him.

So the work of loving God is mostly the work of knowing Him. Spend time with Him and love will come. It is not something you manufacture by effort. It grows the way it grows between people, through time spent together.
You Cannot Trust What You Do Not Love
Then love produces trust, and trust is the hinge of the whole chain.

Trust is not about God's ability. Almost every Christian believes God can. The struggle is about whether God will, and specifically whether He will be good to me. That question is settled by love, not by information.

Think about how it works between people. You do not trust someone because you have verified them. You trust them because you know their heart toward you. A child does not hand her father her hand at a busy road because she has assessed his competence. She does it because she knows he loves her.

That is why the ways of God matter so much to your ability to trust. When you know His ways you know what He is after, and then even His delays and His refusals look different. You stop reading silence as rejection. You stop reading delay as denial. You have enough history with Him to give Him the benefit of the doubt, and that is what trust actually is.
Trust Shows Itself In Obedience
Now watch how trust turns into obedience, because this is where many of us are exposed.

Every act of disobedience is a statement of distrust. When we disobey God we are saying, in that moment, that we know better than He does about what will make us happy. We are saying His way will cost us something we cannot afford to lose. That is the root of it every single time.

Which means the cure for disobedience is not more willpower. It is deeper trust, and deeper trust comes from deeper knowing. If you are struggling to obey in an area, do not only fight the behaviour. Go back up the chain and ask what you believe about God in that area.

Look at Abraham on the mountain again. God asked him for Isaac, the son of the promise, the one he had waited twenty five years for. If Abraham had only known God's works, that command would have been unbearable, because on the level of works it made no sense at all. Why would God give a son and then ask for him back? But Abraham had come to know the ways of God, and the writer of Hebrews tells us what he concluded. He reasoned that God was able to raise Isaac from the dead. Knowing led to trust and trust led to obedience, and obedience took him up that mountain.
Abraham knew, therefore he willingly offered Isaac. Job knew, therefore he could say I know that my redeemer liveth while he was sitting in ashes. Knowing is always underneath obedience.
Obedience Opens The Blessing
And then obedience opens the blessing, which is where God has always wanted to bring us.

I want to be careful here, because this is where teaching goes wrong. God does not bless us as payment for good behaviour. He is a Father, not an employer. But there is a real relationship between obedience and blessing, and it is not transactional. It is more like the relationship between opening a window and letting in air.

God's commands are descriptions of how life actually works, given by the One who designed it. When you obey Him you are living in agreement with the grain of reality instead of against it. Forgiveness releases you. Generosity enlarges you. Purity clears your vision. Honesty gives you a conscience you can sleep on. The blessing is not bolted on from outside, it grows out of the obedience itself, and God adds His own favour on top of that.
Abraham obeyed on the mountain and God confirmed the covenant to him with an oath. The blessing came after the knife was already raised.
There Is No Other Way

The old hymn says it better than I can. There is no other way to be happy in Jesus but to trust and obey. Whoever wrote that line had walked with God long enough to know that there is no fifth option, no clever route around the chain.

I have watched people try to find one. Some try to get the blessing without the obedience, and they burn through years chasing formulas and prophecies and seed offerings, hoping to unlock what only obedience opens. Some try to obey without trust, and they become bitter and religious and exhausted, keeping rules for a God they secretly suspect. Some try to trust without knowing, and their trust collapses the first time life goes hard, because it was built on nothing.
The chain works in one direction only. Know Him, and love will come. Love Him, and trust will come. Trust Him, and obedience will come. Obey Him, and the blessing will come.
So if you want to be blessed, go all the way back to the beginning of the chain and ask for what Moses asked for. Teach me Thy ways, that I may know Thee.
Have I pleased You, Lord? Have I given You joy? Then teach me Your ways.
Come back with me to the tent outside the camp, because there is a conversation happening there that I do not want you to miss.

Moses has pitched a tent away from the people and called it the tabernacle of the congregation, and everyone who seeks the Lord goes out to it. When Moses goes in, the cloudy pillar comes down and stands at the door, and the people stand at their own tent doors and watch from a distance. That detail alone should stop us. The people worshipped from their doorways while one man went inside.
And inside that tent Moses says the thing that has become the cry of my whole life.

lines: And he said unto him, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.

body.text: The Offer Moses Refused
Understand what Moses was turning down, because it makes his prayer far more remarkable than it first appears.

God had already promised to send an angel ahead of them. He had already promised to drive out the Canaanite and the Amorite and the Hittite. He had already promised the land itself, a land flowing with milk and honey, everything that had been sworn to Abraham. Every material item on the list was guaranteed. The only thing withheld was God going with them personally.

Most of us would have taken that offer without hesitation. The land, the victory, the inheritance, the security, all of it, and the only thing missing is the presence. Who would notice? The children would eat. The nation would settle. The promise would technically be fulfilled.
Moses noticed, and Moses refused. He said, if You are not going with us, cancel the whole thing.
And when God agreed, Moses still was not finished. In the same conversation he asked for more.

lines: And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.

body.text: He had face to face conversation, and he asked for the ways. He got the promise of the presence, and he asked for the glory. There was no ceiling on that man's appetite, and I believe that is precisely why God trusted him so far.
The Blessing Or The Blesser
So let me put it to you the way I have had to put it to myself many times.
I do not want provision without the presence. I do not want protection without the presence. I do not want any blessing without the Blesser. I do not want the land without the Lord.
Now hear why this matters, and it is not because provision is bad. It is because provision alone is not proof of anything.

Unbelievers also have food. Unbelievers also have shelter and clothing and cars and holidays and healthy children. There are men who have never prayed a day in their lives who are richer than every person in your church put together. If the whole evidence of your walk with God is that you are fed and clothed, you have no evidence at all, because the man who denies God is fed and clothed too.
So what makes the difference? Moses asked exactly that question, and answered it.

lines: For wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth.

body.text: The distinguishing mark of God's people is not their prosperity. It is His presence with them. That is the only thing the world cannot reproduce.
I want more than everyone else has. Not more money and not more comfort. More of Him.
Wanting Is Not A Small Thing
I want to talk to you about desire, because I have come to believe that the level of a person's hunger determines the level of their walk with God more than any other single factor.
David is called a man after God's own heart, and when you read his prayers you see what that means. He was not a balanced man about God. He was extreme.

lines: One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to enquire in his temple.

body.text: One thing. Not one thing among several. One thing, and the rest arranged around it. That is a narrowed life, and narrowed lives go deep.

God responds to hunger. He always has. He fills the hungry with good things and He sends the rich away empty. If you go to God satisfied you will come back the same way you went. If you go desperate, something happens.

And here is the difficult part. Most of us are not hungry, we are busy. We have crowded our lives so full of good things that we have no appetite left for the best thing. Nobody decides to stop wanting God. We just get full on other things and then wonder why prayer feels like a duty.

So if your hunger has died, that is what to pray about first. Ask Him to make you hungry again. That is a prayer He delights to answer, and I have prayed it myself in dry seasons more times than I can count.
Lord, I want You. I want more. More, more of You.
When He Becomes The Light
There is something that happens when a person begins to want God like this, and it is very hard to explain to someone who has not tasted it.
When I look into His loveliness, everything around me becomes a shadow in the light of Him.

The things that used to control me lose their grip, not because I fought them into submission, but because I saw something better. That is how deliverance actually works most of the time. You do not stop wanting the lesser thing by staring at it and resisting. You stop wanting it because your eyes filled up with something greater and the lesser thing simply lost its colour.

Ambitions that used to drive me look small next to Him. Offences that used to consume my thinking look petty. Fears that used to keep me awake look manageable, not because the danger changed, but because I am looking at Him and not at it.
Paul knew this, and he wrote about it from the middle of real suffering.

lines: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.

body.text: Notice he calls it light affliction. This is a man who was stoned, beaten, shipwrecked, imprisoned and left for dead, and he calls his suffering light and momentary. He was not minimising his pain. He was weighing it against a glory so heavy that his suffering looked light on the scale.
That is what happens when you see Him. Everything else gets weighed correctly.
The Promise Attached To The Presence
And do not miss what God attached to the presence when He finally answered Moses.

lines: And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.

body.text: My presence, and I will give thee rest. The two come together in one sentence. The rest that the wilderness generation never entered, because they never knew His ways, is the very thing God hands to the person who has His presence.

You have been trying to find rest through arrangement. If this problem is solved, then I will rest. If that money comes, then I will rest. If this child settles down, then I will rest. And every time one of those is settled another rises up in its place, because rest was never on the other side of your circumstances. Rest is on the other side of His presence.
So stop negotiating with your circumstances and start seeking His face. I want You, Lord. I want more of You. And with You comes the rest I have been chasing in every other direction.
Let me ask you three questions that have no reasonable answers.
How can a shout bring down a wall?
How can singing break open a prison?
How can a wooden rod part a sea?

There is no engineering in any of it. Israel marched around Jericho for seven days and on the seventh day they shouted, and stone walls thick enough to build houses on collapsed outward. Paul and Silas sat in a Roman jail with their feet in stocks and their backs torn open, and at midnight they sang, and the foundations of the prison shook and every door opened and every chain fell off. Moses stretched a stick over the Red Sea and the water stood up.
God's ways are unfathomable, and that is not a weakness in them. That is where their power lives. The way of God is the way of power precisely because it does not depend on what is available to us.
I choose the way of the Lord.
The Divine Exchange

Now, if you follow the ways of God through scripture, you find a pattern that repeats so consistently that you can build your life on it. God does not remove hard things from His people. He converts them.
Watch the exchange:

lines: There may be pain, and there is gain on the other side of it.
There may be weakness, and out of it comes strength.
There is a cross, and after the cross there is a crown.
There is bitterness, and He turns it to sweetness.
There is loss, and He brings restoration.
There is death, and He answers with resurrection.

body.text: That is the way of God. He did not spare His own Son from the cross, He raised Him from the dead. He did not keep Joseph out of the pit and the prison, He brought him out of the prison into the palace. He did not stop Job's losses, He restored double. He did not prevent the three Hebrew men from entering the furnace, He walked in there with them and they came out without the smell of smoke.

Understand this and you will stop panicking when hard things come. The presence of trouble in your life is not evidence that God has left the room. It may be the very material He intends to work with.
All Things, Not Some Things
This is the promise that holds the whole pattern together, and you must have it in your bones.

lines: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

body.text: All things. Not the pleasant things. Not the things that make sense. All things. The betrayal, the diagnosis, the closed door, the delay, the loss you could not explain. Every one of them is being made to work, and they are being made to work together, which means the pieces that look wrong on their own are being fitted into something.
Paul said the same thing about his own imprisonment.

lines: For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

body.text: I know that this shall turn. He did not say it might turn. He said he knew, and he was in chains when he said it.
Job said it too, sitting in ashes with his children buried and his body covered in sores, with nothing at all in his hand to support the statement.

lines: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth.

body.text: I know that my redeemer liveth. Where did Job get that certainty? Not from his circumstances, because his circumstances said the opposite in every direction. He got it from knowing God's ways. He knew who God was, so he knew how the story would end even while he was in the worst chapter of it.
And I have come to tell somebody reading this page that the sun is shining again. I know your God will turn things around.
Laughing At Storms
There is a passage in Job that describes the settled person, and I want you to see the last word in it.

lines: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee. In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword. Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh. At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh.

body.text: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh. That is not denial and it is not bravado. It is the composure of someone who knows how God works.
You will laugh at storms when you know His ways. You will laugh at destruction when you know His ways. You will laugh in famine when you know His ways. You shall have no fear when you know His ways.

The person who only knows God's works cannot laugh in famine, because her confidence is in the visible supply and the supply has failed. The person who knows God's ways has seen Him work from nothing before, so an empty cupboard does not frighten her the way it once did.
This is the practical dividend of everything I have been writing about. It is not academic. It shows up on the day the report comes back bad.
A Word For The Weary
Now let me speak to some of you directly, because I know who is reading.

You have been fighting battles back to back. One thing has hardly finished before the next one started, and you are tired in a way that sleep does not touch. Hear the word of the Lord over you. Rest is coming. The house of the enemy is growing weaker and weaker and you are waxing stronger and stronger, and it will not always look the way it looks today.
I will bring you into all round rest, says the Lord. Even now your warfare is accomplished.

And there is someone finding love after years of loneliness. You have watched everyone else and you have done the arithmetic on your own age and concluded that your time has passed. Forty eight years. Fifty two years. It is never too late with God. Nothing is impossible with Him, and He is not governed by your calendar.

Somebody has been afraid to hope again because hope has hurt before. I understand that fear and I am not going to scold you for it. But I am asking you to bring that fear to the God whose ways include resurrection. He does His best work in places that everyone else has written off, and He has never yet run out of ways.
Choose The Way Of Power
So when you look at the situation in front of you and there is no reasonable way through, remember the shout at Jericho and the singing at midnight and the rod over the sea.
Your situation does not need to be reasonable to be resolved. It needs God, and God has ways of working that have never occurred to you and never will.
That is why I keep saying it, and I will keep saying it until the last page. The way of God is the way of power. I choose the way of the Lord.

In November of 2021 I stood before a gathering of women in Port Harcourt and told them that the word over that season was face to face. I said it then and I have not stopped saying it, because I believe it is what the Father is saying to His church.
Here is where it comes from.

lines: And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.

body.text: Face to face. Not through a prophet. Not through a dream that needed interpreting. Not through a message passed down through three people before it reached him. Face to face, the way you speak to someone sitting across the table from you.
That is what is on offer, and most of God's people have settled for something much less.
The Face That Shone
Now watch what that kind of fellowship did to Moses, because this is the part that should provoke us.

lines: And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.

body.text: Moses wist not. He did not know. He came down the mountain with light coming out of his skin and he had no idea. That is the first thing to see about carrying the glory. The one carrying it is the last to notice, and that is exactly how it should be. It is others who should see the shine on your face.
Anyone who is announcing their own glory does not have much of it. The genuine article does not need a press release.

lines: And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.

body.text: They were afraid to come near him. And eventually they asked him to cover it.

lines: And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses' face shone: and Moses put the vail upon his face again, until he went in to speak with him.

body.text: Put a veil over your face before you talk to us. The people could not bear the glory on a man who had been with God.

So let me ask you some uncomfortable questions. What does your presence command? Are unbelievers comfortable around you? How about carnal and worldly Christians, are they at ease when you walk in? Do people cover their faces in shame when you appear, or does nothing change in the room at all? And here is the sharpest one. Does your own presence convict you of sin?

I am not talking about being harsh or strange or unfriendly. Jesus carried more glory than any man and children climbed on Him. I am talking about a weight, a substance, something that comes into the room with you that did not come from you.

I think of Kathryn Kuhlman, a woman whose meetings were marked by a presence so heavy that people wept before a word was preached. She had paid a price in private that showed in public, and the shine on her was not something she manufactured on the platform.
What The Glory Cost Moses
Somebody will read all this and want the shine without asking what it cost, so let me give you the figures.
Moses went up to Mount Sinai eight times. He did not go once and settle for the memory.
Moses fasted forty days and forty nights, and not once. Three separate times. The Bible records that he went without food or water for a hundred and twenty days in the presence of God.
And here is what all of that produced in his body.

lines: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.

body.text: A hundred and twenty years old, and his eyes were still clear and his strength had not left him. Spiritual stamina has a way of affecting physical strength. The man who spent a hundred and twenty days without food in the presence of God was still strong at a hundred and twenty years.

So I pray for you now. As your years, so shall your strength be, in the name of Jesus. Your eyes will see physically because your spiritual eyes are alert, in the name of Jesus. And I pray that spiritual hunger will douse physical hunger in you. Lord, bring us to Your table, that like Elijah we may partake of food that carries us forty days and beyond.
Moses was satisfied with the presence of God. He abided. He was not in a hurry to leave. He stayed long enough that the glory permeated every tissue of his body.

Most of us are in a hurry. We give God the leftover fifteen minutes of a crowded day and wonder why nothing rubs off. You cannot spend real time with God and have the glory not rub on you. The problem has never been the availability of the glory. The problem is the length of our stay.
My Own Testimony
Let me tell you something from my early days, and I tell it not to boast but so you know I am writing about something I have tasted.

In the years just after my conversion I used to take my annual leave from work and spend it on retreat with God. Not holiday. Not visiting family. Alone with Him. I had just come out of a two week prayer with one request, and the request was this. Oh God, make me a terror to the kingdom of darkness.

God answered that prayer, and the answer showed up in ways I did not expect. People ran from me on the street. Old men and women bent down to greet me. Some younger people would suddenly cross to the other side of the road when they saw me coming. I had not said a word to any of them.

I am not telling you that story so you will admire me. I am telling you so you will know it is possible. It is possible to walk in the glory of God. It is possible to carry a heavy presence of God with you twenty four hours a day, seven days a week. And it is available to more than the famous few.
The Greater Glory Coming
Now lift your eyes, because what Moses walked in was one realm of glory and there is a greater one coming on the church.

lines: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts.

body.text: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former. Greater glory. And I believe it will be a combined glory, a coming together of the former and the latter in one house, because God says He will set His hand again the second time to recover His people.

lines: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.

body.text: What will that look like? I believe we will see cancers dropping off bodies. Healing by shadows the way it happened with Peter, and by handkerchiefs the way it happened with Paul. Nations being born in one day. Reapers overtaking sowers, so that the harvest comes in faster than the seed goes down. Limbs growing out. Body organs replaced, kidneys, breasts, hearts, brains restored by the hand of God.

And I will tell you something about that last one that most people miss. The sickness that is afflicting you right now may be developing compassion in you to heal that very same sickness in others. God wastes nothing, not even your affliction.

So let me ask you the question I asked those women in Port Harcourt. Are you ready? Are you really ready? Are you expectant of the coming glory? How are you preparing for it? Are you set, are you positioned?
Because glory does not fall on the unprepared and stay.
Come Up Closer
And now let me tell you what I hear in the heart of the Father, because this is the reason for the whole book.
I hear Him yearning. I hear Him saying, come closer. Come up closer, Mary. Come, Esther. Come closer.

He is calling names. He called for Adam in the garden and said, where art thou, and He has not stopped asking. He is calling your name right now. Where are you? I cannot hear you. I cannot see you. Come up close.
I long to fellowship intimately with you, He says. I want to talk to you as a man speaks to his friend, face to face.
I want new friends. I want friends to stand where Abraham stood, and where Moses stood, and where David stood, and where Kathryn Kuhlman stood. Come up close, pastor's wife. Come.

lines: After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter.

body.text: Come up hither, and I will shew thee. There is much more He wants to show you, and the showing happens up close.
What Is In His Heart
Hear the Father speaking, because this is the burden of it all.

I want to give you more than miracles. I want to make you a miracle worker. I want to make you the sign and the wonder. I want to show you My ways, and in My ways are the very miracles you have been seeking.
You are seeking for what is in My hand. There is much more in My heart for you. I have good plans in My heart for you, better plans than the ones you are pursuing.

lines: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

body.text: I know what I am doing, He says. I have it planned out, plans to take care of you and not to abandon you, plans to give you the future you are hoping for.
Stop seeking My hand. Seek My heart. Stop seeking My works. Seek My ways.

Only trust Me. Whatever you are going through, I know it. I permitted it, to bring you to My expected end of intimate fellowship with you. It shall turn to good for you. It shall turn to your salvation, your enlargement, your increase, your prosperity and your healing.
And if you doubt His willingness, settle it with this one verse and never raise the question again.

lines: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?

body.text: I did not withhold Jesus, He says. I gave Him to you. I sacrificed Him for you. What again can I not give you?

lines: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

body.text: Seek first, and all these things shall be added. The things you have been running after are listed under added. Go after the kingdom and the additions will catch up with you.
Cheer up. Hold on. Keep on keeping on. All that God must do in you and through you shall be done.

label: Chapter Ten
title: How To Come Face To Face

body.text: You have heard so much about the how by now, and you have heard about the benefits of the presence. So let us finish with the practical steps, because a book that stirs you and leaves you without instructions has not served you.
I have summarised these from James, Matthew and the Psalms, and they are not complicated. They are just costly.
One. Draw Near

lines: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.

body.text: Draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you. Read the order. He responds to our movement. He has already come as far as the cross, and the step that is waiting to be taken is ours.
Come closer. That is the first instruction and the simplest. Stop admiring the presence from the doorway of your tent like the Israelites did while Moses went in. Go in.

Practically this means deciding on the time and the place and defending it. Not when I feel like it. Not when the house is quiet, because the house will never be quiet. Choose the time, tell your family, and keep it the way you would keep an appointment with someone important, because you are.
Two. Cleanse Your Hands
Cleanse your hands, He says. Hands speak of what we do, our conduct, our dealings, our practice.

To have clean hands is to be blameless in your dealings, to have done no wrong that is sitting unaddressed. It is the business you conduct honestly. It is the money you did not touch. It is the person you wronged and went back to make it right with.

Some of us are praying long prayers with dirty hands and wondering why heaven seems quiet. There is a matter God has already told you to settle, and you have been asking Him for fresh revelation instead. He will not give you new light while you are ignoring the last light He gave.
Three. Purify Your Heart
Then purify your hearts. Hands speak of conduct, and the heart speaks of what nobody sees.

A pure heart is a heart cleared of envy, bitterness, unforgiveness and malice. It is possible to have clean hands and a filthy heart. You have not done anything to her, but you cannot stand her. You have not spoken against him, but you would not be sorry if he failed.
Look at what is promised to the pure in heart.

lines: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

body.text: They shall see God. If seeing God is the whole aim of this book, then this is not an optional chapter of your life. Impurity of heart is not just wrong, it is blinding. Bitterness will cost you your sight of Him faster than almost anything else.

lines: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully. He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

body.text: Who shall ascend? The question is asked and then answered, and the answer is not about gifting or title. Clean hands and a pure heart. That is the qualification for the hill of the Lord.
Four. Be Single Minded
Do not be double minded. Be single eyed. Be sold out. Die to self. Burn your bridges behind you.

lines: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.

body.text: Double minded people are unstable, and James says plainly that such a person should not think he will receive anything from the Lord. That is not harshness, it is physics. A man trying to walk in two directions arrives nowhere.

When God becomes your focus, you will become His focus. When God is number one in your heart, you will be number one in His heart. Make Him your priority and watch what He does with the rest of your life.
Five. Put Fire On Your Altar
Every believer has an altar, and every altar either has fire on it or it does not. Put fire on your altar. Add wood to your fire.
Intensify your prayer life. Not longer prayers for the sake of length, but real dealings with God. Prayer is where you learn His ways, because it is where you hear Him.
Intensify your study. Nobody knows the ways of God who does not know the word of God. His ways are recorded there, in the way He dealt with people over thousands of years.
Intensify your meditation on the word.

lines: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

body.text: Intensify your worship. Be a worshipper, not just a singer. Worship brings you face to face faster than anything else I know, because worship takes your eyes off yourself and puts them on Him, and that is the whole point.
Prayer and study will show you God's ways. Worship will bring you to His face.
Six. Watch Your Company
There is one more, and it is the one people resist most.

Remember what happened in John chapter six. Jesus began to talk about deep things, about fellowship and intimacy and eating His flesh and drinking His blood, and the shallow minded multitude left. They were fine while there was bread.

There are people you do not need in your life. There are people you should not be spending your hours with. People who are satisfied with fish and bread and nothing more. I am not telling you to despise anyone or to become proud, and I am not telling you to abandon the people God has given you to carry. I am telling you to be honest about who is pulling you forward and who is holding you still, and to spend your time accordingly.
You are on a different journey now. You are on your way to talking with God face to face, and not everyone is going that way.
What Face To Face Looks Like
So how will you know it is working? Let me describe it.
Face to face, you have no time for little things, small things, mundane things, things that do not advance the kingdom of God. Your appetite changes.
Face to face, gossip has been dropped. And if you must gossip, sister, gossip the gospel.
Face to face, anger is gone, and malice and unforgiveness followed anger out of the door.
Face to face, I am no longer a slave to sin. I am a child of God.
Do not keep this to yourself. Take somebody's hand, a sister or a brother, and pray for them right now, that they will begin to experience God face to face.
Why Elijah Was So Confident
I want to close with a prophet and a question.
Why was Elijah so bold when he walked into the palace of a wicked king with no army and no backing and said this?

lines: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.

body.text: According to my word. Where does a man get the confidence to shut the heavens over a nation by his own word?

Elijah had come to the realm where God's word and his word were the same. The message and the messenger had become one. He could speak in God's stead because he knew the ways of God so thoroughly that he was not guessing.

Notice the phrase in the middle of that verse. The LORD God of Israel, before whom I stand. He was speaking to Ahab but he was standing before God. That is a man who lived face to face, and the boldness came out of the standing.
That realm is not closed. God is bringing us into the realm of power with Him, the realm of the extraordinary and the supernatural. He is bringing us into intimate fellowship as we draw near to Him.
The Last Word

Do you want contentment in your life? Do you want serenity? Maybe it is peace you have been looking for. Rest, stability, sufficiency, contentment. You can find all of these and much more when you know the ways of God.

And it is automatic that if you know His ways you will also know His deeds. While Israel was contented with the miracles, Moses busied himself being the miracle worker. The one who knows the ways ends up seeing more of the works than the one who chased the works ever did.
So this is my prayer for you as you close this book.

lines: May we know Him today.
May we know and experience the power of His resurrection.
May we also know the fellowship of His sufferings.
May we know His ways.
May we, through knowing His ways, also know His works.
May we leave this page determined to draw closer to Him.
May we leave this page resolved to seek His ways, and to become obsessed with His ways.

body.text: Of all the knowledge this world offers, none surpasses the knowledge of God. You too can know Him. You too can be reconciled to Him. It is possible to know God's ways.
Oh God, if You are pleased with us, teach us Your ways, that we may know You.

Let everything in our lives become a shadow in the light of You. Let all that matters in my life be Jesus. Jesus only, Jesus ever, Jesus all we need. Saviour, Sanctifier, Healer, Baptiser and Coming King.
Father, bring us face to face in fellowship with You, in the name of Jesus.
You are powerful, so powerful in Your ways. You are glorious, so glorious in Your ways.
